predecessors.name: Timurid Empire
predecessors.text: Timur's imperial capital Samarqand and Tashkent, where Khalil Sultan 'proclaimed himself emperor' soon after Timur's death in February 1405

successors.name: Timurid Empire
successors.text: Samarkand and Transoxiana, taken back by Shah Rukh in May 1409 and, after the 1449-1451 rivals, by Abu Sa'id Mirza in June 1451

ledger.x: 18 February 1405: Khalil Sultan takes Timur's throne in Transoxiana.
1405: Khalil Sultan holds Transoxiana against Shah Rukh at Herat, who 'marched his army out of Herat to the Oxus river but made no offensive move against his nephew at this point'.
13 May 1409: Shah Rukh enters Samarkand unopposed and ends Khalil Sultan's rule.
October 1449: Abdal-Latif Mirza overthrows and has his father Ulugh Beg killed, and rules Samarkand.
9 May 1450: Abdal-Latif is killed at Samarkand and his cousin Abdullah Mirza, whom he had imprisoned, becomes ruler of Samarkand.
June 1451: Abu Sa'id Mirza takes Samarkand and executes Abdullah Mirza.

wars.name: Timurid war of succession of 1405-1409 (Shah Rukh against Khalil Sultan)
wars.outcome: After 'a series of unproductive negotiations as well as many military encounters' the war 'started to turn in Shah Rukh's favour' in 1409; Samarkand 'was taken unopposed by Shah Rukh' on 13 May 1409.

wars.name: Timurid civil war of 1447-1451 (Ulugh Beg, Abdal-Latif, Abdullah Mirza, Abu Sa'id Mirza)
wars.outcome: Abdal-Latif's 1449 revolt killed Ulugh Beg and led to 'civil war'; Abdullah Mirza held Samarkand from May 1450 until Abu Sa'id Mirza defeated and executed him in June 1451.

certainty.note: The Khalil Sultan page names a title (ruler of Transoxiana) and cities, never a boundary.
The dossier holds no land in these years (Transoxiana is the Timurid Empire's, under Ulugh Beg as governor); the entry only keeps certainty continuous.
Samarkand is certain; the extent of the rivals' Transoxiana is not given by any page.
